description:
A checked-in benchmark harness, a bulk-update session-budget fix, and the profile-backed lock-hygiene change turn every published performance figure into an artifact-backed contract.

## Background

The adversarial audit in `dev/studies/cdc840ad-audit-2026-07-23.md` found every published timing to be a single self-attested measurement with no artifact. `apply_bulk_update` (`commands/bulk_update.rs:161-197`) retains the O(n)-sessions pathology — it opens preflight and publication sessions for every filter-matched issue before knowing whether anything changes (cost 2·|matched|) — while `check_auto_transitions` already demonstrates the correct shape: a cheap Issue-local eligibility prefilter that can only skip, never authorize, plus an authoritative recheck inside the session. Meanwhile zero-byte `.lock` sidecar files accumulate without bound: `load_issue` shared-locks a `<id>.lock` sidecar on every read (`storage/json.rs:918-919`, created O_CREAT at `storage/lock.rs:286-294`, never removed), so a read-all command such as `jit query available` creates one per issue read (692 sidecars observed for 665 issues).

The lock-hygiene design was decided during planning from the committed session-cost profile `dev/studies/perf/session-cost-27ffbd2d.json`: the sidecar originates on the shared read path, so even lazy creation still grows O(issues), and the sidecar read lock is therefore eliminated. Issue JSON is published by atomic temp+rename, writers serialize on `.jit/.repo-write.lock`, and `list_issues` already holds `.index.lock` shared around its load loop, so `load_issue` can read directly (or, as defense-in-depth, take the shared lock on the existing repo-scoped `.index.lock`). The surviving fixed lock set is O(1) — roughly six files independent of issue count — and orphaned sidecars are deleted once as cleanup, not correctness.

The benchmark harness `scripts/benchmark-session-cost.sh` builds the release binary, generates a fixture repository, and times each scenario with warmup and repeated measured runs, emitting one JSON artifact at the stable path `dev/studies/perf/session-cost-<jit-commit>.json` with machine, cache-state, and corpus metadata; `session-cost-27ffbd2d.json` is the first instance and the schema template. Every published timing must cite artifact path, command name, and stat.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-09: A checked-in benchmark harness records repeated runs with machine and cache-state metadata as artifacts at a stable path, and every published timing claim traces to such an artifact.
- [hard] REQ-10: Session-open budget tests bound bulk update to eligible work, matching the guarantee already tested for automatic transitions. The bound is C·|matched issues that are not provable no-ops|, with C derived from a single-issue baseline run rather than hardcoded.
- [hard] REQ-11: The per-session cost profile is recorded as an artifact, and the lock-hygiene approach chosen from that profile is implemented so zero-byte lock files no longer accumulate without bound. The per-issue sidecar read lock is eliminated, the surviving lock set is O(1) in issue count, and orphaned sidecars are cleaned up once.

## Notes

The lock-hygiene decision is pinned by plan decision PD-1: eliminate the per-issue sidecar read lock, keep the O(1) fixed lock set, decided from `dev/studies/perf/session-cost-27ffbd2d.json`. Every `load_issue` caller must be checked before removing the sidecar lock, since a reader relying on it for more than torn-read protection would be a regression; atomic temp+rename already prevents torn reads. Budget tests count session opens via the existing `TransactionFailurePoint` probe, deterministic and machine-independent. Cache-state contract is warm-only; timings are comparable only across artifacts sharing the same measurement filesystem.
title: Establish an artifact-backed performance contract
